name: Kaddora Newsletter – Email Campaigns, Newsletter Builder & Automation
author: kaddora

sections.description:
Kaddora Newsletter is a WordPress newsletter and email marketing plugin. Its standard edition can be installed and activated without purchasing Kaddora Newsletter Pro or entering a Kaddora license key.

The standard edition includes email campaign creation and sending, subscriber management, signup forms, double opt-in, three starter templates, a visual email builder with four standard elements, optional campaign scheduling, CSV import and export, campaign analytics, and consent-based WooCommerce opt-in. Trigger-based automation and additional integrations are available only in the separately installed Pro add-on. The functionality included in the standard edition does not expire.

Upgrading to Kaddora Newsletter Pro is optional. Users who need additional advanced capabilities may choose to upgrade. Purchasing Pro is not necessary to install, activate, or use the functionality included in the standard edition. No Kaddora account is required to use the plugin.

Email delivery uses WordPress’s wp_mail() function and the site’s configured mail transport. Newsletter records are stored in local WordPress database tables. Open and click tracking are disabled by default and can be enabled by an administrator.

Privacy and data retention

Kaddora Newsletter registers a personal-data exporter and eraser in Tools > Export Personal Data
and Tools > Erase Personal Data. These cover subscriber records, signup fields, queued message
records, tracking events and the plugin’s WordPress user consent timestamp. Deleting a subscriber
from the plugin also removes their queued messages and tracking events. After the selected retention
period, sent-message recipient addresses and message content are cleared while a minimal token,
subscriber and campaign record is retained to keep older one-click unsubscribe links working.
Failed/skipped queue records and tracking events are removed; subscriber contacts are not deleted
automatically. The plugin adds suggested privacy-policy text when the
WordPress privacy policy editor is available. Site administrators remain responsible for ensuring
that their privacy policy, mail transport and consent practices match their use of the plugin.

Features

  • Create and send email campaigns using WordPress wp_mail() and the site’s configured mail transport.
  • Manage subscribers, add contacts, import contacts from CSV, and export subscriber data.
  • Create newsletter signup forms with generated form-specific shortcodes.
  • Double opt-in subscription confirmation.
  • Three starter newsletter templates are available in the standard edition.
  • Visual email builder with four standard elements: Heading, Text, Hero, and Button. Includes layers, responsive preview, undo/redo, JSON import/export, and test email.
  • Campaign queue, optional scheduling, and batch sending through wp_mail().
  • Campaign analytics and configurable open and click tracking. Tracking is disabled by default.
  • Optional consent-based WooCommerce checkout opt-in; the checkbox is unchecked by default and requires an affirmative customer choice.
  • Unsubscribe handling and signup consent controls.
  • Standard-edition functionality does not expire and does not require a Kaddora account or Kaddora license key.
  • Upgrading to Kaddora Newsletter Pro is optional for users who need additional advanced capabilities.

Website Shortcodes

Use a WordPress Shortcode block or Elementor Shortcode widget.

Signup form: Copy the form-specific shortcode from the Forms screen.
Starter template: [kaddora_newsletter_template slug=”welcome-welcome-onboard”]
Saved template: [kaddora_newsletter_template id=”123″]

Copy the actual ID or slug from Forms or Templates. Templates display newsletter designs;
forms collect subscribers. Neither template shortcode sends an email. Editing a starter
creates a saved copy; use that saved template’s ID shortcode to display your edits.

External services

This plugin does not require a Kaddora account and does not send newsletter subscriber
data to a Kaddora-operated service.

  • Email delivery uses WordPress’s wp_mail() function. Actual delivery is handled by the
    site’s configured mail transport or SMTP provider. When an administrator sends a
    campaign, the recipient address, subject and message content are passed to that
    configured mail transport. If the separately installed Pro add-on is used for trigger-based
    automation, its email actions also use the same configured mail transport. Review that
    provider’s terms and privacy policy before enabling delivery.
  • Email tracking is disabled by default. If an administrator enables open or click
    tracking, the plugin records the recipient ID, campaign ID, event type, click destination
    (for clicks), and event time in this site’s WordPress database. Open tracking uses a one-pixel
    image; click tracking redirects through this site’s URL. Administrators should disclose
    tracking to recipients and follow applicable privacy law. Completed queue records and event
    history are automatically purged after the configured retention period (180 days by default;
    configurable to 90, 180, 365 days, or retained indefinitely). Subscriber records remain until
    an administrator deletes them or a privacy erasure request is processed.
  • The free edition’s optional WooCommerce integration adds an unchecked newsletter-consent
    checkbox to checkout. It captures a billing email only when the customer actively checks
    that box. The integration uses local WooCommerce hooks and does not call a WooCommerce
    remote API. The plugin stores the subscriber email, source and consent timestamp.
  • The separately installed Pro add-on provides optional consent-based integrations for
    WordPress Users, Contact Form 7, WPForms and Fluent Forms. These use local WordPress/plugin
    hooks and do not call those products’ remote APIs. The WordPress Users integration adds an
    optional registration checkbox. For Contact Form 7, WPForms and Fluent Forms, the form owner
    must add a checkbox whose field name identifies newsletter, subscribe, marketing, consent
    or opt-in. Only submissions with an explicitly checked consent field are considered.
    The integration stores the subscriber email, name when provided, source, consent timestamp,
    and pending/subscribed state; it does not retain the complete third-party form payload.
  • When double opt-in is enabled, contacts captured by WooCommerce or the Pro integrations
    receive a confirmation email and remain pending until the confirmation link is submitted.

No third-party API key is required by this plugin’s current implementation. The site
privacy policy should explain subscriber storage, configured mail transport, optional
integrations, and whether open/click tracking is enabled. Review the applicable provider
terms and privacy policies before enabling services. Useful provider information:
* WordPress: https://wordpress.org/about/privacy/
* WooCommerce: https://woocommerce.com/terms-conditions/ and https://automattic.com/privacy/
* Contact Form 7: https://contactform7.com/privacy-policy/
* WPForms: https://wpforms.com/privacy-policy/
* Fluent Forms: https://fluentforms.com/privacy-policy/
* WordPress.org plugin directory guidelines: https://developer.wordpress.org/plugins/wordpress-org/detailed-plugin-guidelines/

Free and Pro edition

The WordPress.org edition contains the complete free subscriber, signup form, campaign, sending, tracking, CSV import/export and free builder workflows. Premium element implementations, editable Pro starter templates, trigger-based automation execution and the additional WordPress Users, Contact Form 7, WPForms and Fluent Forms integrations are not included in this package. The standard edition retains the consent-based WooCommerce opt-in integration. The Pro template gallery in the free edition contains catalog metadata and static preview images only. Premium functionality is provided by a separately distributed Kaddora Newsletter Pro add-on that must be manually installed by the site administrator.
sections.installation:
1. Upload the “kaddora-newsletter-email-campaigns-newsletter-builder-automation” folder to “/wp-content/plugins/”, or install the ZIP through Plugins > Add New Plugin > Upload Plugin.
  2. Activate Kaddora Newsletter from the Plugins screen.
  3. Open the Kaddora Newsletter menu and configure your sender information, signup forms, subscriber settings, and email preferences. The standard edition can be used without purchasing Pro or entering a Kaddora license key.
  4. Test email delivery with a test email before sending a campaign.
  5. Add a signup form to a page using the shortcode shown for your saved form in the Forms screen.

Campaign sending and cleanup use WordPress Cron. On low-traffic sites, scheduled jobs can run late;
for time-sensitive sending, configure a real server cron to trigger wp-cron.php and monitor the queue status.

Import only contacts who have given appropriate permission to receive your newsletter. Review your site’s privacy policy, configured mail transport, consent settings and local laws before enabling tracking or integrations.
sections.faq:
Do I need to purchase Kaddora Newsletter Pro to use the standard edition?

No. You can install, activate, and use the functionality included in the standard edition without purchasing Pro or entering a Kaddora license key. Pro is optional for users who need additional advanced capabilities.

Does the standard edition expire?

No. The functionality included in the standard edition does not expire.

Do I need a Kaddora account?

No. A Kaddora account is not required to install, activate, or use the plugin.

Can I create and send newsletter campaigns in the standard edition?

Yes. The standard edition lets you create and send campaigns using WordPress wp_mail() and your site’s configured email delivery system.

Can I manage subscribers and signup forms?

Yes. You can manage subscribers, add contacts, import and export CSV files, create signup forms, and use double opt-in confirmation.

Is upgrading to Pro compulsory?

No. Upgrading is optional. You can continue using the functionality included in the standard edition without purchasing Pro.

How is email delivered?

The plugin sends messages through WordPress wp_mail(). Actual delivery is handled by the mail transport or SMTP provider configured for your site. Check that provider’s terms, privacy policy, and pricing.

Is open or click tracking enabled automatically?

No. Open and click tracking are disabled by default. A site administrator can choose whether to enable them.
sections.changelog:
1.0.0

  • Initial WordPress.org release of Kaddora Newsletter.
  • Includes subscriber management, signup forms, double opt-in, CSV import/export, campaign creation, scheduling, batch sending, and optional local campaign tracking.
  • Includes three editable starter templates and four working email-builder elements.
  • Pro catalogue entries contain static preview metadata and images only; premium implementations are distributed separately.
  • Includes privacy exporter/eraser support and migration-safe storage.
